# Capability map

Headlines only: each `Cn` is a capability, with the count of Requirements that specify it. Requirement bodies are not rendered here — read them with krill's `get_feature_slice` / `get_requirement_slice` MCP tools, or re-render with detail.

## Now

- **C1** — A Requirement Contributor can record a product's spec as structured entities — product, feature set, feature, functional and non-functional requirement — instead of as prose in a file. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C2** — A Requirement Contributor can attach a load-bearing decision to the feature set it constrains, so whoever touches that area is shown it and nobody loads the global list. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C3** — An Agent can ask krill for exactly the spec slice its work touches — one feature set, one feature, the requirements beneath it — without reading the whole product. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C4** — An Agent can do that from whatever harness it is running under — Claude Code today, omnigent or whagent-net next — without a per-harness integration being written for it first. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C5** — A Requirement Contributor can see what any requirement or decision said at an earlier point in time, and what superseded it. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C6** — A Requirement Contributor can amend a shipped spec by superseding it rather than overwriting it, so shipped history is never rewritten. (4 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C7** — Anyone can read a product's current spec as generated, read-only repo docs — the product doc set only — that are split and indexed automatically, with krill remaining the only writable source. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C8** — A Swarm Operator can import an existing markdown-specified product into krill and confirm nothing was lost in the move. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C9** — A human can cross-link a PR, commit, or conversation to a krill product through a thin GitHub pointer artifact, as they do today. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C32** — A Requirement Contributor can resolve a deferred Non-Goal (2 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C33** — A Requirement Contributor can void a mistaken create (2 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C34** — A Swarm Operator can plan and transition a milestone without a status collision (4 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C35** — A persona dispatched through a krill plugin gets a working, discoverable tool surface that matches the plugin's own docs and schema (delivery/plugin defect triage) (0 FR, 6 NFR)
- **C36** — Every spec-axis kind and delivery record krill holds is reachable and truthfully described through its published surface, and the checks that verify that surface actually run (2 FR, 7 NFR)

## Next

- **C10** — A Requirement Contributor and an Agent can hold a design session in krill, with each draft revision kept as a record instead of a comment thread plus a gist. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C11** — Anyone can query what is still open in a design session — blocking versus non-blocking questions, answered or not — rather than re-reading the thread to find out. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C12** — A Requirement Contributor can submit an idea or user story in plain language and have a producer-role Agent shape it into conforming entities on their behalf, so intake is forgiving while the spec layer stays rigid. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C13** — A Requirement Contributor can cut a product's spec into shippable milestones and agent-shippable milepebbles, so *what* and *when* are tracked on separate axes. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C14** — An Agent can claim an available task and receive a payload self-contained enough that it never has to supplement it by reading the spec surface. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C15** — An Agent can report what happened on a run without knowing where the task goes next. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C16** — An ephemeral Agent can be picked up on any host and resume a task from the references krill holds, without re-discovering context the last run already had. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C17** — A Swarm Operator can answer "what is claimed, what is stuck, what dead-lettered, and why" from a console. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C18** — A Swarm Operator can intervene on a stuck or thrashing task — requeue, cancel, release a lease, escalate to a human — without hand-editing storage. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C25** — Any persona can record scope they noticed but are not acting on as a tracked note with its own lifecycle, instead of leaving it as a stray comment somebody has to find. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C26** — A Swarm Operator can leave a swarm running unattended. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C27** — A Swarm Operator can bring in a product krill did not author and have krill render it back faithfully, so the model is shown to generalize past its own author. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C28** — A Requirement Contributor can see, from krill alone, what is planned versus what is merely spec'd, including work that is only partially complete. (2 FR, 3 NFR)
- **C29** — A Swarm Operator can do everything M5's console/intervention set offers (what's claimed, stuck, dead-lettered, and why; requeue/cancel/release/escalate) from a browser instead of an MCP/API client. (6 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C30** — A Requirement Contributor can submit, browse, and answer a design session — including C12's mediated intake path, never a form that writes FRs directly — from a browser instead of an MCP/API client. (5 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C31** — Anyone can browse a product's live spec (capability map, load-bearing decisions, personas, non-goals) and delivery/roadmap status (C13/C28) from a browser, replacing "read the rendered docs" with a live queryable view. (4 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C37** — The ops console and the specs it renders report failures, fields and citations the way krill's own requirements say they do (0 FR, 3 NFR)
